title: Micro postmortem: KV-cache evictions + degraded tail latency (short notes)
content:
Context:
- Night shift (00:15-04:30). Short, focused notes for handoff/next steps — not a full postmortem.
- Incident triggered by spike in 95/99th token-latency for hosted API customer requests hitting model shards on gpux-pool-4.

What I observed (high-level):
- 00:43: first PagerDuty alert: "serving-runtime.kv-cache.evictions > 1200/min" and accompanying tail-latency SLO alert (95p > 450ms) for route /v1/generate-redwood-16k.
- CPU on lookaside-cache-controller pods increased, KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~92% -> ~46% over 8 minutes.
- Autoscaler did not create new gpux nodes fast enough because burst-capacity pool policy was mis-tagged; route fell back to cheaper model-variant which increased tokens-per-request.

Immediate mitigation actions I took:
- 00:47: scaled up cache-controller replica from 2 -> 4 (kubectl scale deployment cache-controller -n serving --replicas=4).
- 00:50: manually scaled gpux-pool-4 node-group +3 nodes in GCP (console action), put a note in the pager channel.
- 01:05: temporarily pinned routing policy for the busiest customer to their dedicated model-variant (reducing model-switch churn).
- 01:12: flushed a small prefix cache entry that was hot but corrupt (kubectl exec -c admin cachectl -- /usr/bin/cache-tool evict --key=prefix:abcd1234). Confirmed hit-rate improvement by 01:20.

Preliminary timeline (rough):
- 00:40: latent evictions grow after background compaction job kicked off (log snippet: compactor started at 00:39:52, delta bytes=+1.2GB).
- 00:43: Pager alert firing.
- 00:50: scaling up controller + node group requested.
- 01:20: 95p latency back to ~220ms, cache hit-rate ~88%.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Background compaction job (newer compaction binary rolled Friday) temporarily increased memory pressure and triggered aggressive eviction policy. New compactor version reduces conservative TTLs -> higher churn.
2) Routing autoscaler tag bug prevented burst capacity from being used quickly, causing more requests to fall to slower variants and amplifying tokens.
3) Corrupt prefix/metadata for one customer produced repeated cache misses for a large prefix key (investigated and evicted).

Evidence to collect (next):
- compactor binary version and rollout history (k8s rollout history compactor-deploy).
- detailed evictions per-key histogram from 00:30-01:30 (metrics: serving.kv.evictions.bucket).
- autoscaler audit logs for gpux-pool-4 (who changed tagging policy and when).
- Compare tokens/request histogram across variants for the impacted customer.

Runbook / action TODOs (assign owners):
- [ ] update compactor rollout checklist to include canary retention flag (owner: Samir) — SRE-789.
- [ ] add an alert to detect "compactor started + >500 evictions/min within 5m" (owner: Maya).
- [ ] fix autoscaler tag mapping for burst-capacity (owner: infra-team, ticket INC-4321).
- [ ] add a small e2e test that simulates compaction under medium memory pressure so we catch eviction policy regressions in CI (owner: Noah).
- [ ] document manual eviction command sequence in runbook (owner: Emilia) — update runbook: /confluence/serving/kv-cache-runbook (placeholder).

Quick notes to hand off:
- Watch gpux-pool-4 for 2x24hrs; if compactor evictions spike again, consider rolling compactor back to previous image.
- Customer X sees more 5xxs during incident window; notify CS with timeline + mitigation performed.

Incident followups for postmortem (deferred):
- Full timeline with traces (collect IDs: trace ids appended in slack thread).
- Root cause writeup: confirm if compaction change introduced TTL/eviction change or if it was the autoscaler tag timing.
- SLA impact calc: tokens and requests lost/added cost estimation.

Misc commands & snippets (copyable):
- Check cache hit-rate per pod: kubectl top pod -n serving | grep cache-controller; curl -s http://pod:9090/metrics | grep serving_kv_hit_rate
- Evict suspect key: kubectl exec -it deploy/cache-admin -n serving -- cache-tool evict --key=prefix:abcd1234 --confirm
- Get compactor rollout info: kubectl rollout history deploy/compactor -n infra --revision=

Open questions (for Monday sync):
- Who merged the compactor config that reduced conservative TTLs? (PR #? — link needed)
- Why did the autoscaler tag mapping diverge from the deployment descriptor? Was there a config drift from terraform?

Handoff summary (for next oncall):
- Status: stable for now, 95p latency recovered to ~220ms at 01:20.
- Primary next step: finish compactor binary audit and revert if regression confirmed.
- Keep watch on evictions metric and gpux-pool-4 autoscaler events.

Personal notes:
- Write a short runbook snippet describing the quick eviction workflow (this literally saved ~25m).
- Try to automate the small prefix detection query used during the incident.

-- Emilia
